why: in is the preposition, not inches: qalc on its own reads it as a unit and answers in cubic metres
a bare f is Fahrenheit, not farads
a bare k is kelvin only when the other side is already a temperature
one number, not a mixed-unit sum: without conv none this reads 11 lb + 0.369810 oz
the hero carries the rate, which is what stops the next four queries
a temperature carries no rate: a scale with an offset does not have one
a quantity with no target still offers its own family
a word that is not a unit answers nothing rather than qalc's guess at it: qalc -t firefox is 0 B
